title: Bidirectional A* in Reykjavík: Faster Routes!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* carve a shortest path across Reykjavík’s real street layout by searching from both the start and the goal. The two frontiers meet in the middle, dramatically reducing explored nodes while preserving optimality.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Reykjavík’s streets turned into a graph—now watch **Bidirectional A*** zoom in! 

In this visualization, every intersection becomes a **node** and every road segment becomes an **edge** with costs (distance/time). **Bidirectional A*** runs **two A*** searches simultaneously: one forward from the start and one backward from the goal, each guided by a consistent heuristic like straight-line distance. 📍📍 When the frontiers collide, we reconstruct the optimal route—often exploring far fewer nodes than one-directional A* while still targeting the shortest path.

❄️ Real-map twist: street networks are irregular graphs (non-uniform connectivity, one-ways if modeled, and varying block geometry). By meeting in the middle, the algorithm adapts to those complexities more efficiently, especially when the start and goal are far apart.

👉 Want a Part 2 with different heuristics or edge weights? Drop a 🔥 and comment “REYKJAVIK” and I’ll build the next one!
